title: traffic quarantine policy and rollback safety-netting for staged upgrades
creator: Alex Chen
description: Introduce a 'traffic quarantine' policy and associated automation to reduce blast radius during staged model/runtime upgrades. The quarantine policy is a lightweight routing/flagging layer that isolates suspicious cohorts to a limited execution pool and applies conservative rollback rules. This ticket covers design, implementation, and a rollout plan for: 1) cohort scoring rules (anomaly detectors + heuristics), 2) quarantine routing and dedicated capacity fallback, 3) automated rollback conditions and cooldowns, and 4) operator-visible runbooks and dashboards. Goal: reduce false-positive rollbacks while containing real regressions quickly and predictably.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic can be dynamically marked as quarantined by score or rule without redeploying the service
Quarantined cohorts run on configurable isolated pool with lower concurrency and preserved KV cache behavior
Rollback automation triggers only when weighted health score exceeds threshold and persists to operator-visible incident with suggested remediation
Dashboards surface quarantine counts, per-cohort scores, and rollback triggers with links to PRs and prompt-sets used for quality checks
Playbook exists and is validated during a simulated canary (drill) with no customer-visible downtime
runbook: Step 0 - Detection: anomaly lambda produces cohort score (0-100) using p99 latency delta, error_rate, generation_error_rate, and evaluation regression metric over last 10 minutes
Step 1 - Quarantine: cohorts with score >= 60 are marked quarantined; routing policy tags traffic metadata and routes to quarantine pool (dedicated small instance group)
Step 2 - Mitigation: quarantine pool enforces conservative generation settings (max_tokens cap, lower concurrency) and toggles strict model variant fallback
Step 3 - Alerting: trigger 'quarantine-created' incident with automated triage checklist (link to telemetry and related PRs)
Step 4 - Auto-Rollback: if weighted health score remains >= 75 for 5m and user-visible error_rate > configured SLO-burn, trigger automated rollback to previous model/version and escalate to on-call
Step 5 - Recovery: after rollback, run synthetic prompt-set evaluation; quarantine is released only after automated checks pass and operator confirms
implementation_notes: Will augment smart routing layer to accept 'quarantine' flag in routing key and support a small dedicated instance pool for quarantined traffic
Cohort scoring service will reuse existing telemetry pipeline; add new aggregation for 'quality_regression_score' derived from evaluation harness and prompt-sets
Rollback automation will be implemented as an idempotent orchestration job with dry-run and audit log; it must emit a confirmation event to avoid flip-flop
We choose score thresholds conservatively to avoid noisy quarantines; initial rollout will use a higher threshold and be tuned after two weeks of data
Trade-off: quarantining reduces exposure but can increase latency for those cohorts due to conservative execution settings; we will document this in the console and on the API response header

qa_plan: Stage 1: unit tests for scoring logic and routing tag propagation
Stage 2: integration test with quarantine pool and cache-affinity in staging (use real model snapshot)
Stage 3: run 'canary-drill' where we inject a synthetic regression and verify quarantine + rollback behavior end-to-end
Stage 4: monitor live traffic with quarantine thresholds set to conservative mode for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and adjust thresholds
